item.title: How to Update n8n Self-Hosted: Safe Upgrades for Docker Compose, Docker, and npm (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Updating self-hosted n8n is where most self-hosting horror stories start: a skipped backup, a jumped migration, a dead credential set. This guide shows the safe update path for all three install methods, Docker Compose, plain Docker, and npm, with the exact commands, the pre-update backup routine, and the rollback procedure from n8n’s own documentation. It is written for anyone already running n8n on their own server, and pairs with our guide to installing n8n on an Ubuntu VPS and our Docker Compose setup walkthrough if you set things up with our tutorials.

item.title: n8n Docker Compose Setup: Self-Hosting with Postgres and Queue Mode (2026)
item.description:
Introduction

Docker Compose is the way n8n’s own team ships production deployments, and it is the only install path n8n guarantees going forward. This guide builds a complete, production-ready docker-compose.yml for n8n: Postgres as the database, named volumes for data, a .env file for secrets, optional queue mode with Redis workers for heavier workloads, and a safe upgrade routine. It works on any host with Docker, from a $6 VPS to a homelab box. If you need the full VPS walkthrough with a domain and HTTPS in front of this setup, read our guide to installing n8n on an Ubuntu VPS first, it ends exactly where this article begins.
